clue.text: Ultimate in misbehaviour when class briefly admits a naughty child

indicators.note: the ultimate letter of a word is its last, so this picks the end of misbehaviour

parts.note: when and as can both mean 'at the time that'

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the shortened class takes the letter a inside it

parts.note: cl. is the dictionary abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: A teacher notes that a pupil sneaking into a cut-short lesson is the ultimate bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous youngster, a scamp, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: About to introduce tax break

indicators.note: introduce means the about word comes first, before the tax

parts.note: re means about, concerning
cess is an old word for a tax or levy

explanation.surface: A government plans to bring in a tax break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tax break' reads as one phrase, but 'tax' gives CESS and 'break' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess is a pause or interval, as in a parliamentary or school holiday.

clue.text: Operation initially supervised by man on board small boat

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of supervised

parts.note: the king is a chess piece, a man on the board
a raft is a simple flat vessel

explanation.surface: A procedure overseen at first by a man on deck in a dinghy.
explanation.definitionFit: A skin graft is a surgical procedure, transplanting skin to cover a wound or burn.

clue.text: Point pedant raised, boxing clever

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
boxing means the two words enclose the letters wanted

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pedant raises a point while boxing cleverly.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'boxing clever' as the definition, but 'boxing' is the hidden-word signal (the words box the answer) and 'clever' alone defines; in a down clue 'raised' reads TPEDA upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Adept means skilled or proficient, close in sense to clever.

clue.text: Strike breaker at centre of riot near American plant

parts.note: a scab is a worker who crosses a picket line

indicators.note: the centre of a four-letter word is its middle two letters, here from riot

explanation.surface: A blackleg gets caught up in the middle of a riot close to an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike breaker' points to industrial disputes, not botany; the plant only arrives with the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabious is a wild flower with pincushion-like blue heads, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Pounds collected in foreign country by me, helping to make a pile

indicators.note: collected in means the pounds are gathered inside the country

parts.note: Congo is a country in Africa
l is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
taken as written
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: Someone abroad gathers money to help build a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a pile' suggests getting rich; 'to make' is a link and 'a pile' is a heap.
explanation.definitionFit: A conglomeration is a mass of things gathered together, a heap.

clue.text: Associate having academic qualification in education on top

indicators.note: on top in a down clue puts the qualification above the academic

parts.note: BEd is the Bachelor of Education degree
a fellow is a senior member of a college

explanation.surface: A colleague holds a teaching degree and a senior post as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedfellow is a partner or ally, someone one is associated with.

clue.text: Sailor on island heading north for port once

parts.note: OS stands for ordinary seaman

indicators.note: in a down clue heading north means read upwards

parts.note: an ait is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: A seaman on an island sets off north for a port.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the ancient harbour city of Rome at the mouth of the Tiber.

clue.text: During function, food supplier's extra job

indicators.note: during places the food supplier inside the function

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
a deli supplies food; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A caterer's second job is working at functions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' suggests a catered event; here it is the maths function.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideline is a secondary occupation, work done alongside a main one.

clue.text: Decoratively spread icing over top, covering a small cake

indicators.note: covering means the anagram wraps round the other letters
spreading something decoratively rearranges it, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A baker spreads icing over the top of a little cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decoratively spread' rearranges ICING OVER TOP; that anagram covers A and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A Victoria sponge is a jam-filled sponge cake named after Queen Victoria.

clue.text: London theatre's cornier production, containing sex

definitions.note: the possessive here is 'London theatre is', standing for the name

indicators.note: containing means the rearranged letters hold the sex word inside them
a production makes something new out of the material, so the letters of cornier are reworked

parts.note: it is an old euphemism for sex appeal or sex itself

explanation.surface: A critic says the West End theatre's staging is rather corny, though it has a sex scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production' sits naturally with a theatre, but it is the anagram signal; 'it' as sex is an old euphemism, as in the 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Criterion is a theatre at Piccadilly Circus in London's West End.

clue.text: Went courting? That's rather old-fashioned

definitions.meaning: past tense of going out with someone romantically
describes something out of date, behind the times

explanation.definitionFit: To date is to go out romantically; something dated has fallen out of fashion.

clue.text: Lose energy and get one form of it back

parts.note: gas is one form of energy, as in a gas bill

explanation.surface: Someone flagging is told to take a fuel back to restore their energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers to energy, so 'one form of it' is GAS, reversed by 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to droop or flag, which is what tired people do when their energy runs low.

clue.text: Youngster has real recollection about everything, with this

definitions.text: Youngster has real recollection about everything, with this

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: read as re-collection, gathering the letters of real together again in a new order

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about
all means everything

explanation.surface: A child with perfect memory remembers everything that ever happened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollection' looks like the definition but is the anagram signal, turning REAL into ALRE; the whole clue then describes the perfect memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Total recall is the ability to remember every detail, which the clue describes as real recollection of everything.

clue.text: Old emperor is brought in by weird revolutionary once leader's deposed

indicators.note: being brought in by means the word is goes inside the other piece
a revolution turns something round, so the shortened word is read backwards
once its leader is deposed, the first letter is removed

parts.note: freak can mean weird or abnormal, as in a freak storm

explanation.surface: A historical note on an emperor toppled by a strange revolutionary once the leader is overthrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once leader's deposed' leaves REAK; 'revolutionary' turns that to KAER. 'Old emperor' fits the surface's history, making 'revolutionary' read as a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaiser was the title of the German and Austrian emperors, the last of whom abdicated in 1918.

clue.text: Specially choose record that's currently available

parts.note: a single is a record with one main track
out means released, available now

explanation.surface: Pick a record that's been released.
explanation.definitionFit: To single out is to select one for special attention.

clue.text: Once curse builder installing only half of lift

parts.note: a mason is a builder in stone

explanation.definitionFit: Malison is an archaic word for a malediction, the opposite of benison.

clue.text: A guy's gone berserk in place of worship

explanation.definitionFit: A synagogue is a Jewish house of prayer.

clue.text: Trawl round pier regularly for fish

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of pier

explanation.surface: Fishermen trawl round the pier for a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trawl' suggests fishing; here it means search.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea perch are various marine fish resembling perch, such as the bass.

clue.text: Country more in the red, we're told, after introduction of euro

indicators.note: after puts the sounding piece behind the opening letter
the introduction of a word is its opening letter, here from euro
we're told signals a word that is heard rather than seen

parts.note: stony means penniless, so stonier is more broke, deeper in debt

explanation.surface: A nation found itself deeper in debt after it adopted the euro.
explanation.walkthrough: STONY (as in stony broke) means penniless; STONIER, said aloud, gives STONIA. Estonia did adopt the euro, so the surface is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic state, the northernmost of the three, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Arguing can be a sport

propelling a boat with oars, a competitive pastime (rhymes with go)

explanation.definitionFit: The same spelling covers a quarrel (row as in 'cow') and oarsmanship (row as in 'go').

clue.text: Men on short time engaged in work with corporation

OR, other ranks, means enlisted men

explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is an old jokey word for a paunch, not a company.

clue.text: Period of success, growing variety of broccoli here?

clue.text: Strange, meeting bachelor at a dance

parts.note: rum means odd, strange

explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Noted players in good condition, securing first place in league
